newsitem.title: INDIA: India call down, gilt yields fall on brisk buying.
newsitem.headline: India call down, gilt yields fall on brisk buying.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday around 10.65 percent after touching a high of 10.90 percent during the day, dealers said.
It opened in the 10.50-10.85 percent range and trading throughout the day was dull on low volumes, they said.
"The bulk of the deals were completed in the morning and then the market was quiet," a dealer at a foreign bank said.
Prices of government securities in the secondary market firmed as trading volumes rose, dealers said.

"It is quite surprising as normally securities are not much in demand when call money rates are high," a dealer said. "But some banks seem to be building up positions in short-term assets anticipating a cut in cash reserve requirements and a consequent fall in interest rates," he said.

The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock was traded on Wednesday at 13 percent against Tuesday's 13.15 percent while the 13.50 percent 1998 stock was traded at 13.37 percent against 13.44 percent, dealers said.
There was little activity in certificates of deposit (CDs) and commercial paper, dealers said.
"Banks are quite comfortable on the deposits front," said a dealer. "There is little interst in CDs."
Commercial paper was quoted around 13 percent for top-rated companies, dealers said. Rates on intercorporate deposits were steady in the 17-19 percent range for top-rated companies, they said.
